operations.title: GET /api/tasks: optional status filter and counts by status
operations.body_md:
`GET /api/tasks` returns every task, including cancelled and done ones, so the landing page and other public consumers miscount open work.

## Acceptance criteria
- `GET /api/tasks?status=open,ready` returns only tasks whose `status` is in the comma-separated list; without the parameter the response is unchanged.
- Unknown status values give HTTP 400 with a JSON error naming the invalid value(s) and the accepted ones.
- The response carries a `counts` object with the number of tasks per status (computed before filtering).
- Unit tests cover: no filter, one status, several statuses, an unknown status (400) and the counts.
- `npm test` passes; docs/API or README mention the parameter.

## Restrictions
- No secrets in code or tests; no change to MCP tools.

task.instructions_md:
# Status filter for GET /api/tasks

In `src/worker.js` (route `/api/tasks`), accept an optional `status` query parameter (comma-separated). Validate each value against the statuses the catalog uses; unknown -> 400 JSON error. Add `counts` (per status, before filtering). Add tests under `test/` with the existing test style (`node --test`). Run `npm test`.

acceptance.text: GET /api/tasks?status=a,b returns only tasks with those statuses; no parameter keeps the current response.
Unknown status values give HTTP 400 naming the invalid and the accepted values.
Response includes counts per status, computed before filtering.
Tests cover no filter, one, several, unknown (400) and counts; npm test passes.

restrictions: No secrets in code or tests
